mil3.3.12:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of consciousness?”
mil3.3.12:1.2: “The characteristic of consciousness, Great King, is cognizing.”
mil3.3.12:2.2: “Suppose, Great King, a city watchman sitting at the central crossroads of the city were to see a man coming from the east, were to see a man coming from the south, were to see a man coming from the west, and were to see a man coming from the north;
mil3.3.12:2.3: in the same way, Great King, whatever a person sees as a visible form with the eye, he cognizes it with consciousness.
mil3.3.12:2.4: Whatever he hears as a sound with the ear, he cognizes it with consciousness.
mil3.3.12:2.5: Whatever he smells as an odor with the nose, he cognizes it with consciousness.
mil3.3.12:2.6: Whatever he tastes as a flavor with the tongue, he cognizes it with consciousness.
mil3.3.12:2.7: Whatever he touches as a touch with the body, he cognizes it with consciousness; and whatever he cognizes as an idea with the mind, he cognizes it with consciousness.
mil3.3.12:2.8: That, Great King, is how consciousness has the characteristic of cognizing.”
